bole.text: Moderately buttressed (TTSM); 'grandes gambas delgadas', large thin buttresses (src 3); short buttresses sometimes reaching 3 m (Wikipedia, src 1, gives the height). Useful Tropical Plants says the bole branches from low down.

crown.text: Wikipedia: rounded crown, a common canopy tree. Useful Tropical Plants (src 2) says elongated crown instead.

phenology.fruit: brown, flat, obliquely obovoid-oblong one-seeded pod about 5 cm long

bark.text: Smooth grey bark, pink inner bark (TTSM); 'corteza gris y lisa' (src 3); smooth, light grey on old trees (Wikipedia).

habitat.range: Southern Pacific Costa Rica (Osa, Golfo Dulce) and Panama; Wikipedia adds the Atlantic coast of Colombia.

notes: Leaves: one pair of leaflets (occasionally three), elliptic-lanceolate, long acuminate, leathery, 5-8 x 3-4 cm (TTSM); Wikipedia gives leaflets 5-7 x 2-3 cm. Phenology is Osa-specific: Vilchez (1997, cited in TTSM) at Mogos, Osa: intensive leaf fall Jan-Feb, leaf flush mainly Mar-Apr, flowers May-Aug (peak June), mature fruit Nov-Jan. Allen (1956, cited in TTSM): briefly deciduous late Dec/early Jan, brown leaves conspicuous before falling, new foliage almost immediately, the flushing tree visible for many kilometres (flush colour not given); flowers early Aug-Sep, fruit early Feb. Wikipedia: flowers Aug-Dec, fruit Nov-Feb. leafless_months [1] is my reading of 'briefly deciduous'; no source gives a leafless month count. Fruiting is not annual: mast crop Feb-Mar 2000 after little or no fruit 1995-1999 (src 4). Shade tolerance from src 3: high sapling survival in shade, high mortality in sun, poor regeneration in gaps (the paper does not use the word). dbh typical is the adult-population mode at Mogos (70-80 cm class, src 3); max 1 m from TTSM and Useful Tropical Plants. Height max 50 m from src 1 and src 3; TTSM 35-40 m. TTSM and Useful Tropical Plants call it deciduous. No source read names animals eating its fruit, seeds or leaves; src 4 discusses seed predation only generally.
